label: Bibliographic
what: Authors, year, title, venue, DOI, publication type.

label: Country / countries
what: Country or countries of the study, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, comma-separated if multi-country. If only a region is named, record the region verbatim and leave codes blank.

label: Setting
allowed: school, PHC, community, online, mixed, other, not reported
what: Primary delivery setting. Use 'other' with free-text detail in notes when none fit; 'not reported' if the source does not state it.

label: Sample size
what: Analysis sample if reported, otherwise enrolled (flag which in 'basis'). For reviews: number of primary studies and pooled participants.

label: Population age band
what: Report the age band as in the source, then map to 10-19, 10-24 and 18-24 where extractable. The 18-24 mapping lets records be filtered to the evaluation study population.

label: Study design
allowed: RCT, non-RCT trial, cohort, cross-sectional, qualitative, mixed-methods, SR, SR+MA, scoping, umbrella, framework, regulatory, other
what: Study design; use the closest single category.

label: Intervention / object type
what: e.g., single-LLM chatbot, rule-based chatbot, hybrid, digital SSI, app, SMS, other. Free text; be specific.

label: Review question(s) addressed
what: Which review streams this record speaks to. Assign all that apply; this drives which thematic groups are worth extracting.

label: Outcomes or properties reported
what: Outcomes or properties reported, verbatim from source where possible.

label: L&MICs flag
what: TRUE if the study setting is a low- or middle-income country by World Bank classification at study midpoint. Used to gate Stream 1c.

label: SSA flag
what: TRUE if the study setting is in Sub-Saharan Africa.

label: South Africa flag
what: TRUE if the study setting is South Africa.

label: Evidence-type tag
what: One-line label for the kind of evidence, e.g. 'validation study', 'ecological audit', 'framework paper', 'meta-analysis of RCTs'.

label: Funding / conflict of interest
what: Intervention funder(s); research funder(s); COI declaration.

label: Open-access status
what: TRUE if the record is open-access (for the reproducibility record).

label: Minimal quality flag
what: Soundness-only minimal quality appraisal per RR §5.1. Base on reporting completeness and basic risk-of-bias signals; 'not appraisable' when the record type does not support appraisal.

label: Effect size on primary MH outcome
what: For the primary mental-health outcome: type of estimate (Cohen's d, SMD, OR, risk difference), point estimate, 95% CI, follow-up window, outcome instrument, and direction of effect.

label: Effect size by outcome domain
what: One row per outcome domain: depression, anxiety, distress, wellbeing, goal-progress, help-seeking, mental-health literacy. Add extra rows for any other mental-health outcomes reported.
feeds_eval: Eval §7 (PHQ-8, GAD-7, WHO-5, K-10, GBO, ORS secondaries)

label: Effect trajectory and durability
what: Effect estimate and 95% CI at each reported assessment point, with exact time since intervention completion. Whether the effect was maintained, increased, attenuated, disappeared, reversed or remained uncertain relative to the preceding assessment and the immediate post-intervention effect; latest time point at which benefit was observed. Distinguish within-group change from between-group effects.

label: Uptake rate
what: Proportion of invited/eligible users who start the intervention; the denominator must be specified.

label: Session-completion rate
what: Definition of 'completion', numerator and denominator, and the arm-level completion rate.

label: Attrition — mid-session
what: Where in the flow users drop; per-stage attrition where reported; and qualitative explanations for stopping, skipping, or incompletely engaging with the intervention.

label: Acceptability instrument and score
what: Acceptability instrument (e.g., SUS, AAQ, CSQ-8, custom), the score, the score range and any threshold used.

label: Overall user experience and acceptability
what: Themes on overall helpfulness, relevance, ease of use, conversational quality, perceived empathy, burden, privacy, trust, satisfaction, and willingness to use or recommend the intervention.

label: Engagement definition and indicators
what: How engagement was conceptualised or measured: time on task, number of sessions or turns, depth of response, intervention completion, action-step formulation, emotional involvement, return visits.

label: Action-step uptake evidence
what: Proportion formulating and reporting attempts to implement an action step; timing; types of action selected; and qualitative accounts of whether and how action steps were attempted, helpful or feasible.

label: Re-entry / return-visit patterns
what: Proportion returning; time to return; reasons for returning or not; circumstances prompting re-entry; how participants and authors interpreted repeat use.

label: Variation in experiences and outcomes
what: Differences by age, gender, language, location or other relevant characteristics; quantitative subgroup findings and qualitative differences in experiences or explanatory themes.

label: Modality and delivery format
what: Chatbot (rule-based / conversational / LLM / hybrid), mobile app, SMS, web module, IVR, VR, other; text, audio or multimodal delivery; (a)synchronous interaction.

label: Therapeutic approach
what: CBT, behavioural activation, cognitive restructuring, mindfulness, safety planning, growth-mindset, self-compassion, IPT, other; and whether there is explicit single-session-intervention (SSI) framing.

label: BEST-element analogue present
what: For each BEST element — Brain science (B), Empowerment (E), Saying-is-believing (S), Testimonials (T) — yes/no with an evidence span. Note any other design parameters used.

label: Session dose, duration and structure
what: Single-session or repeated; intended number, duration and frequency of sessions; number and order of stages or agents; required vs optional components; fixed, user-selected or adaptive sequence; whether users can pause, resume or repeat.

label: Orchestration architecture
what: Workflow-orchestrated, model-orchestrated or hybrid; deterministic vs generative components; model autonomy; content constraints and high-level guardrails.

label: Personalisation features
what: Language-register adaptation, example matching, pacing, memory.

label: Content corpus source
what: Origin of the content corpus (e.g., Project YES US-origin), whether it was adapted, and the method of adaptation.
feeds_eval: Eval Decision box (Project YES corpora portability)

label: Interaction and conversational design
what: Free-text, menu-based or mixed input; open-ended vs constrained dialogue; question and response format; response length; tone, persona and relational style; reflection, summarisation and feedback; opportunities to skip, revise, stop or choose a pathway.

label: Human-support model
what: Fully automated, clinician-supported, coach-supported, peer-supported or blended; role, timing and intensity of human involvement; human review, moderation or override.

label: Engagement-supporting design features
what: Reminders, notifications, prompts, gamification, progress indicators, rewards, goal setting, choice of content, re-engagement messages and other features intended to initiate or sustain participation. (Actual engagement outcomes belong in Stream 1a.)

label: Evidence linking design features to outcomes/UX
what: The specific design feature examined; the comparator where applicable; the outcome/experience linked; direction of the relationship; type of evidence (experimental comparison, observational association, qualitative account or author interpretation); contextual conditions. Reference the relevant 1a record rather than duplicating the result.

label: Co-design and formative development
what: Human-centred, participatory or co-design methods; groups involved; stages and degree of involvement; prototype/usability/cognitive pre-testing; changes made in response to findings.
feeds_eval: Eval Decision box (pre-launch cognitive pre-testing gate)

label: Comparator used
what: Comparator (waitlist / static content / usual care / active digital) with description.

label: Language(s) supported
what: Primary and secondary languages supported; code-switching; reading/ literacy level required; translation/localization process; language- or literacy-related barriers; user comprehension; groups underserved by language options; adaptations made during implementation.

label: Device / connectivity and access
what: Devices used/required; smartphone or feature-phone compatibility; bandwidth and data requirements; offline/low-data functionality; shared-device use; user data costs; electricity/charging constraints; connectivity, device-access or digital-literacy barriers.

label: Recruitment channel and operation
what: Recruitment channels (platform, school, clinic, social media, partner network); how each was implemented; recruitment duration; staff/partner inputs required; reach into the intended population; barriers and facilitators; groups under-reached; modifications to improve recruitment.

label: Consent process for digital MH
what: One-stage or staged process; adult consent, parental consent and adolescent assent requirements; comprehension checks; digital signature or other documentation; age/identity verification; confidentiality concerns; comprehension/acceptability problems; refusal reasons; operational burden; adaptations introduced during implementation.

label: Cultural / linguistic adaptation method
what: Adaptation framework (e.g., Bernal, ecological validity, deep vs surface adaptation); components adapted; stakeholders involved; formative research, co-design or piloting; implementation challenges; participant/provider views on cultural relevance; changes made in response to feedback; reported effects on acceptability, trust, comprehension, engagement or retention.
feeds_eval: Eval §3.4 equity; Project YES corpora decision

label: Referral pathway description
what: Referral trigger; risk threshold; message presented to the user; consent to referral; automated or human review; warm or cold handoff; referral destination; partner acknowledgement; human follow-up; feedback to the platform; operating hours; roles and responsibilities; barriers encountered in operating the pathway.

label: Referral-chain performance
what: Proportion reaching each step of the chain; time to human contact; unsuccessful or delayed referrals; reasons for pathway failure; user and provider experience; corrective actions taken.

label: Recruitment yield / consent rate
what: Numbers approached, screened, eligible, consented, enrolled and randomized; denominator for each rate; yield by channel or subgroup; reasons for ineligibility, refusal or non-enrolment; time to reach the target sample.

label: Retention and attrition at follow-up (L&MIC/SSA)
what: Retention at each assessment point; differential attrition by arm; number/proportion retained at 1, 4 and 12 weeks where available; timing of attrition; reasons for disengagement or loss to follow-up; differential retention by subgroup or channel; reminder/incentive/ human-support/re-engagement strategies and their reported effects; qualitative explanations for stopping or incomplete engagement.

label: Ethics and governance features
what: Ethics/IRB approval pathway; safeguarding protocol; procedures for disclosures of abuse, exploitation, self-harm or imminent risk; crisis detection and escalation; mandatory-reporting requirements; adverse- event monitoring; privacy/confidentiality protections; data storage and residency; data access and sharing; youth-advisory/governance role; operational challenges, delays or failures; changes made in response.

label: Scalability lessons
what: Estimated and actual cost per user; staffing model; partner arrangements; sustainability (e.g., evidence of continued delivery beyond the study period).

label: Implementation contexts
what: Any other reported contexts of implementation such as health, education, social and community-systems contexts; implementation stage.

label: Types of harm reported
what: Unsafe content (self-harm / suicide / eating), over-reliance, privacy, algorithmic bias, iatrogenic distress; source of the AE (self-report, researchers, system logs).

label: Rate of AE / SAE
what: Numerator, denominator, definition, time window; number of affected users and number of events; whether users could experience multiple events; study arm/comparator; subgroup rates; withdrawals attributable to harm; CIs where reported; and whether zero events means none occurred or none were actively identified.
feeds_eval: Eval Annex A (AE thresholds and stopping rules)

label: Failure modes documented
what: Persona drift, sycophancy, hallucination/fabrication, jailbreak, off-script content, crisis-routing failure.

label: Detection methods
what: Human review, LLM classifier, rule-based, user report; and any performance metrics reported.

label: Preventative and responsive mitigation strategies
what: Rule-based constraints, RAG guardrails, content filters, human-in-the-loop, red-teaming, model-update process.

label: Crisis / safety-alert protocol
what: Trigger, escalation, referral, follow-through; whether it was tested in a live deployment.

label: Causality attribution method used
what: How authors distinguished session-attributable distress from concurrent distress.

label: Post-launch monitoring and governance
what: Drift detection, incident register, transparency note, third-party audits; record whether these were operational, planned only, or activated following an incident.

label: Tessa / drift-type failures
what: Instances where an evidence-based design failed after deployment.

label: Equity-related harms
what: Widening of inequities; algorithmic bias against under-represented users (age, gender, language, literacy, disability, ethnicity/race, socioeconomic position, geography, device type, digital literacy or other vulnerability characteristics).

label: Instruments used
what: Each measurement instrument: name, version, item count, response scale.

label: Age-band appropriateness
what: Validated at 18+ / for adolescents / for adults.

label: Psychometric evidence in SSA / LMIC
what: Reliability, factor structure, measurement invariance, MID; the population and language in which it was established.

label: Minimally important difference
what: Minimally important difference: value, method used, population.

label: Feasibility of digital administration
what: Completion rates, floor/ceiling effects, missingness.

label: Mechanism / proximal measures
what: Hope, agency, self-criticism, coping skills, stigma, felt support.

label: Engagement measures
what: Turn count, response depth, dwell time, next-step formulation.

label: Safety / referral measures
what: Chain-step completion, time to human contact, referral acceptance.

label: Translation / adaptation procedures
what: Forward-back translation, cognitive interviewing, cross-cultural validation.

label: Trust and quality measures
what: User-rated trust, perceived competence, therapeutic-alliance scales.

label: Help-seeking patterns
what: By age-band, gender, urban/rural, digital-first vs in-person.

label: Stigma and disclosure norms
what: Family, peers, community; device-sharing implications.

label: Language coverage
what: English, isiZulu, isiXhosa, Afrikaans, Sesotho; code-switching.

label: Gender-specific drivers of distress
what: GBV, early union, menstrual stigma, restricted schooling.

label: Service-availability constraints
what: Referral capacity, waitlists, cost, geographic access.

label: Prior digital MH deployments in SA
what: e.g., Chommie, STARS; lessons on adaptation and engagement.

label: Regulatory / policy context
what: SAHPRA, POPIA, national mental health policy.

label: Reading age / literacy
what: Population estimates; recommended target.

label: Competitor / comparator products
what: Woebot, Wysa, Tess, Therabot, Chommie, ED ESSI, etc.; features, user base, evidence.

label: Entry channels used
what: Search, social, WhatsApp, in-app referral, school/NGO.

label: Trust / uptake determinants
what: Onboarding, transparency, disclosure of AI, endorsements.

label: Search / social behaviour patterns
what: Youth help-seeking online; peak times; language of query.

label: Safety approaches in commercial products
what: Rate-limiting, escalation, disclaimers, age-gating.

label: Regulator / guidance documents
what: FDA, MHRA, EMA, WHO, SAHPRA on AI-enabled MH tools.

label: Data-handling / provider practice
what: Zero-retention endpoints, DPA structures, data-residency.
